links.outcome: Intention to ask ChatGPT higher-risk health questions, ChatGPT knowledge, and trust after brief AI health literacy interventions vs control
links.effect: Both intervention groups had lower intention for higher-risk scenarios vs control (animation M=2.42, images M=2.69, control M=3.12; p<0.001), higher ChatGPT knowledge (p<0.001), and lower trust (p<0.001). No effect on lower-risk intentions (p=0.800).
links.quote: Participants in both intervention groups reported lower intentions to use ChatGPT for higher risk scenarios compared to control (n=205, M=3.12/5, 95%CI: 2.98 to 3.27, p<0.001).

links.outcome: Intention to ask ChatGPT higher-risk questions and knowledge after AI literacy education for consumers
links.effect: Animation and image interventions reduced intention to use ChatGPT for higher-risk scenarios versus control (M=2.42 and 2.69 vs 3.12, p<0.001) and increased knowledge (p<0.001); trust was lower (p<0.001).
links.quote: Participants in the intervention groups had higher knowledge of ChatGPT (p<0.001) and reported lower trust (p<0.001), compared to those in the control group.
